note: The attacker-controlled input string is cleaned of whitespace before parsing, producing a new heap-allocated buffer that is passed to g_uri_split_internal.
The cleaned URI string is scanned to find the scheme, authority, and path components; p advances through the attacker-controlled bytes.
The authority section is delimited by the first '/', '?', or '#' character; the host substring is bounded by path_start.
When the host begins with '[', the code enters the IPv6 literal parsing branch, treating the host as an IP-literal per RFC 6874.
A '%' character in the IPv6 literal is located; addr is a g_strndup'd copy of the host contents between brackets, nul-terminated.

The code reads pct[1], pct[2], and pct[3] without first checking that at least 4 bytes remain after pct. When the '%' is near the end of the allocated addr buffer, these reads can access bytes past the heap allocation, causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ.

addr is a heap allocation of length-1 bytes (length-2 content plus nul terminator). If the '%' appears at offset length-3 or later, pct[1], pct[2], or pct[3] reads beyond the allocated buffer, triggering the ASAN-detected heap-buffer-overflow READ of 5 bytes.
